detail.title: Thermodynamic and Practical Costs of Memory Reliability
detail.summary: Memory reliability and retention time are fundamentally limited by energy dissipation. Our revision incorporates findings that non-equilibrium environments and non-reciprocal couplings modulate Landauer erasure costs, establishing that predictive power in information engines is constrained by available energy and coarse-grained state access.
detail.reason: Revision required to integrate new dissipation bounds and non-equilibrium evidence into the memory reliability model.

detail.title: Thermodynamic Costs of Memory Reliability
detail.question: How do energy costs scale with reliability and retention time in physical memory systems?
detail.reason: Foundations are set; formalizing the scaling relations is required.

detail.title: Thermodynamic and Practical Costs of Memory Reliability
detail.summary: This revision clarifies that memory retention reliability is fundamentally bounded by the available free energy and the coupling strength to the environment. We incorporate new evidence indicating that coarse-graining limits the accessible information, requiring a trade-off between temporal resolution of memory and energetic dissipation.
detail.reason: Systematic revision allows for better integration of coarse-graining constraints into reliability models.
